name: Catania
title: Catania Ship Gauging | Thickness Measurement for Ro-Ro & Cruise
description: Ultrasonic thickness gauging in Catania for ro-ro ships, ferries, cruise ships and cargo vessels alongside: hull, deck and tank measurement for owners.
h1: Ultrasonic Thickness Measurement for Ships Calling at Catania
intro: Catania is the main commercial port of eastern Sicily, with Mount Etna as its backdrop. Ro-ro ships, ferries to Malta and the mainland, cruise ships, bulk carriers and tankers use its quays. A ship is gauged here during a cargo stop, a long turnaround or a lay-by period before it goes to a yard. Atlantis NDT mobilises a thickness measurement team from India to the vessel and builds the visit around the cargo plan or passenger schedule.

highlights.h: Ro-ro ships with regular return calls
highlights.p: Trailer-carrying ro-ro ships return to Catania on fixed rotations, so a deck, ramp and ballast tank programme can be spread over several calls and compiled into one dataset ahead of the docking.

highlights.h: Cruise turnarounds with a fixed clock
highlights.p: Cruise ships spend one day alongside, so the scope is chosen to fit: void spaces, exhaust gas cleaning piping or a group of tanks that the technical team has already made safe.

highlights.h: Gauging before an east Sicily docking
highlights.p: Catania has no large drydock of its own, so owners use the port to measure first and then send the ship to a yard with the steel estimate already agreed.

port.h: The port of Catania and its ro-ro, ferry and cruise traffic
p: Catania sits on the Ionian coast of Sicily, at the foot of Mount Etna, and its harbour is part of the Eastern Sicilian Sea port system together with Augusta. The old harbour in the heart of the city handles passengers and ferries, while commercial quays reach southwards along the shoreline. Approaches are from open sea with no locks or tidal gates to plan around. The volcano matters to ship operators in a small way: ash fall during eruptions can settle on decks and hatch covers, and it occasionally disrupts flights and road transfers, which affects the planning of any inspection.

Traffic is varied. Ro-ro ships carry trailers between Catania and mainland ports, ferries link the city with Malta and other destinations, and cruise ships call on itineraries around the Mediterranean. Alongside this, the port handles general cargo, dry bulk such as construction materials and agricultural products, containers and petroleum products. For an inspection contractor the interesting part is that many ships here follow fixed rotations: the same ro-ro vessel returns on a regular pattern, and its vehicle decks are empty and accessible while it waits for the next sailing.

Seasons affect cruise and passenger work more than commercial work. Cruise calls peak in the warmer months, and ferries to the islands and Malta run fuller timetables in summer, leaving shorter windows. Autumn through spring is when owners move older tonnage to yards, and gauging in Catania at that point feeds directly into the steel estimate. Strong winds from the south-east can make berthing slower for large ships, and anchorage work off the port depends on sea state. Berths for cargo ships are allocated by the port authority, so a ship that is gauged between operations needs its time on the quay arranged through the agent.

facilities.h: Where gauging can take place at Catania
p: Catania is primarily a working port rather than a repair port. Large dockings are normally done at yards elsewhere in Sicily, in Malta or on the mainland, and the port's value for inspection is access to ships between voyages. Ro-ro berths allow work on vehicle decks and ramps while the ship waits for its next sailing. Passenger quays allow cruise turnaround inspections. Commercial quays allow cargo holds of bulk carriers to be gauged once discharge has left them empty and safe to enter.

Gauging scope therefore depends on berth and ship type. On a ro-ro vessel the programme is deck plating, ramp structure, ballast tanks and the sections of hull accessible from inside. On a bulk carrier it is hold frames, hopper and topside tanks and hatch coamings once holds are cleaned. On a cruise ship it is a targeted list of spaces and pipework. For lay-by or idle ships, a longer programme is realistic because the crew is not working cargo and the ship is not under time pressure.
list: Ro-ro and trailer berths: vehicle decks, ramps and ballast tanks of ships on fixed rotations between sailings
Passenger and cruise quays: turnaround-day gauging of voids, tanks and exhaust gas cleaning pipework
Commercial quays: cargo holds, hopper tanks and hatch coamings of bulk carriers and general cargo ships after discharge
Petroleum product berths: small tankers and bunker craft, scheduled with the terminal and the master
Lay-by berths for idle or waiting ships, where a longer gauging programme is practical
Augusta and Messina: nearby ports used when a ship needs a larger yard for steel work after gauging

context.h: Port state control and regulation affecting Catania ships
p: Port state inspections at Catania are carried out by the Italian Coast Guard (Guardia Costiera) through the harbour master (Capitaneria di Porto), under the Paris MoU system. Ro-ro and passenger ships on scheduled routes face the additional EU inspection regime for ships in regular service, so structural defects on ferries tend to come to light quickly. For owners of older ro-ro ships, a recent set of thickness readings is a practical way to show that a deficiency does not reflect general steel condition.

On the commercial side, the EU Ship Recycling Regulation requires ships calling at EU ports to carry an Inventory of Hazardous Materials with a statement of compliance, and a docking is the usual moment to survey and update it. EU ETS and FuelEU Maritime place a carbon cost on emissions that makes fleet renewal decisions more pointed. Bulk carriers and tankers surveyed under the Enhanced Survey Programme need thickness reports in specific class formats, and gauging before the docking keeps the surveyor's time in the yard focused on close-up inspection.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs at Catania
jobs.p: Catania jobs are built around the rhythm of the ship. A ro-ro on a weekly rotation gives a series of identical windows, a cruise ship gives one fixed day, and a bulk carrier gives the hours after discharge. We agree the scope with the superintendent in advance, record readings against the class thickness measurement formats and return one report that the owner, the yard and the surveyor can all use.
list: Staged gauging of a ro-ro ship's vehicle decks and ramps across several Catania calls ahead of a special survey
Hold and hopper tank gauging on a bulk carrier after discharge, with results sorted by frame for the surveyor
Owner's condition gauging of a ferry before a sale, taken while it lies idle between summer seasons
Scrubber piping wall-thickness readings on a cruise ship during its turnaround day
Pre-docking steel estimate for a general cargo ship that will go to a yard elsewhere in Sicily or Malta

logistics: Catania Fontanarossa airport lies close to the city and the port, with connections to mainland Italy and several European hubs, which keeps transfers straightforward once the team has landed. The crew travels from India on Schengen visas, so dates need confirming once the ship's schedule is known and visa lead time has been allowed. The ship's agent obtains port access and ISPS passes, and we send the equipment list and personnel details to the agent in advance.

faqs.q: Can a ro-ro ship be gauged between sailings at Catania?
faqs.a: Yes, when the vehicle decks are clear and the crew has made tanks safe. A ro-ro on a fixed rotation gives repeating windows, so we plan a block of spaces for each call and merge the readings into one report. The superintendent and the agent confirm the schedule so the team is aboard when the deck is open.

faqs.q: Is there a drydock in Catania for steel renewal after gauging?
faqs.a: Catania is mainly a working port and has no large drydock. Ships needing steel work usually go to a yard elsewhere in Sicily, Malta or the Italian mainland. We gauge here first so that the steel estimate and the renewal list are ready before the ship reaches the yard.

faqs.q: How do you handle volcanic ash on decks?
faqs.a: Ash fall is occasional and mostly affects planning rather than technique. If ash has settled, surfaces are cleaned before readings are taken so the probe couples properly to clean steel. Eruptions can also disrupt flights and roads, so we allow slack when arrival dates are fixed.

faqs.q: Can cargo holds of a bulk carrier be gauged during discharge?
faqs.a: Not safely while cargo is being worked in the hold. The practical window is after discharge, once the hold is swept or washed, ventilated and cleared for entry. We coordinate with the master and the agent so the team starts as soon as the space is released.
